draft.title: Aims, hypotheses, models and theories
card: Aim
a statement of what a study is trying to find out. It says what is being investigated, not what the result will be.
Hypothesis
a prediction of the result, which can be tested. It is written before the data are collected.
Model
a simplified picture, often a diagram, that shows how parts of a process fit together and helps explain what is observed.
Theory
a broader explanation of why something happens. It is built from evidence and can be tested, supported or revised.
draft.remember: Aim: what is studied. Hypothesis: the predicted result. Models and theories: explain what is seen.

a.q: Which statement is a hypothesis rather than an aim?
opts: Teens who sleep 9 hours will recall more words than at 5
To investigate how sleep length affects memory for words
To find out whether sleep and memory are linked in teens
To examine the effect of sleep on how well teens learn
a.why: Only the first option predicts a result, saying which group will recall more. The others say what will be investigated, so they are aims.
a.clue: Which one predicts an outcome instead of only naming a topic?

b.q: Dr Nguyen draws a diagram showing how information moves from sensory input to short-term storage and then to long-term storage. What is this diagram best described as?
opts: A model of memory that simplifies how parts fit together
A hypothesis that predicts how many items will be recalled
An aim that states what the memory study will investigate
A theory that proves why every person forgets information
b.why: A diagram showing how parts of a process fit together is a model. It is not a hypothesis, as it predicts no result. A theory does not prove anything: it explains and can be revised.
b.clue: Think about what a simplified picture of a process is called.

a.best: Teens who sleep 9 hours will recall more words than at 5

b.best: A model of memory that simplifies how parts fit together

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'Only the first option predicts a result', but the options are shuffled. The hypothesis is not necessarily first (here it is second), so a student reading the why could be pointed to an aim.
The hypothesis option 'Teens who sleep 9 hours will recall more words than at 5' is ungrammatical and unclear. It should read something like 'than teens who sleep 5 hours'.

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. Why (a) refers to 'the first option' even though the options are shuffled, and the hypothesis option's 'than at 5' is ungrammatical and should be reworded.
